raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Depends on #8734 (which builds on #8049 and #8042), #8060, #7029, #8017, #8031 and #8730 (which builds on #8026). Please review the diff from their merge: [scoped diff](https://github.com/Connor-XY/Megatron-LM/compare/56e57bda3...yx/pstate-c3-tensor-parallel-fallbacks). The merges regenerate the process-group allowlist where it conflicted. Land this after #8737: until training seeds from the grid that `initialize_megatron` builds, stock `pretrain()` calls `model_parallel_cuda_manual_seed` without groups and would warn once per process.

**Why.** `model_parallel_cuda_manual_seed` and `gtp_replica_rank` read the ranks they need from the global `parallel_state` grid when the caller omits its groups, with no warning. The duplicate filters `param_is_not_tensor_parallel_duplicate` and `param_is_not_gtp_duplicate` warn (#8734), but then call the global rank accessors directly. A caller on its own grid got the global ranks with no signal, so these fallbacks could not be removed on a published schedule.

**What.**
- `model_parallel_cuda_manual_seed` without a collection:
  - Omitted TP, EP and expert-TP ranks come from `resolve_process_groups`, which emits a `ProcessGroupFallbackWarning` (deprecated in 0.21, removed in 0.23).
  - Omitted GTP-remat ranks and sizes warn and come from `resolve_gtp_remat_group(None)`, as the layers resolve them without a collection. Those axes stay off when there is no global grid.
  - The global TP, EP and expert-TP groups are resolved only when one of those ranks is missing. A builder that passes them before any global grid exists, like Megatron-Bridge's MIMO builder, keeps seeding.
- The duplicate filters keep #8734's warning, owner and argument names. The TP filter resolves the group through `resolve_process_groups`, and the GTP filter through `resolve_gtp_remat_group`, instead of calling rank accessors. Without a global grid the GTP filter still keeps every parameter.
- `gtp_replica_rank` resolves `dp_cp`, or `expt_dp` for a routed-expert weight, through `resolve_process_groups` when `parallel_state` is initialized. It returns 0 in a single-process save, and raises `RuntimeError` when there is no group to elect a writer over, as before.
- `VocabParallelEmbedding`, `ColumnParallelLinear` and `RowParallelLinear` read the replica group of their GTP shards from the collection field instead of `getattr` with a default. An unset field still stamps no group, and checkpointing then takes the warned fallback.
- The checker goes from 171 reads to 162. Twelve accessor reads go away. Six become 3 guarded `resolve_process_groups` calls. The other 6 are GTP-remat reads that now go through `resolve_gtp_remat_group` in `process_groups_config.py`, which the checker exempts, so it no longer counts them.

The optimizers that `get_megatron_optimizer` builds and the training parameter statistics already pass their groups and do not warn.

**Tests.**
- New `tests/unit_tests/tensor_parallel/test_tensor_parallel_group_fallbacks.py`, on 4 ranks:
  - helpers given their groups read no global group and do not warn;
  - each fallback warns once and gives the same RNG states and ranks as the global accessors;
  - the seed's GTP-remat axes are off without a global grid;
  - `gtp_replica_rank` without a grid raises;
  - the layers stamp the replica group of their collection.
- #8734's duplicate-filter tests in `test_optimizer_fallback_warnings.py` now patch the groups the filters resolve, not the rank accessors they no longer call. `test_grad_norm_gtp_invariance.py` stops patching names that `layers.py` no longer imports.

On 4 GPUs, an earlier version of these commits on a base without #8734 and #8730 showed no regressions once the `test_grad_norm_gtp_invariance.py` fix above was in. With the other process-group changes from #6307 applied, the full unit test suite shows no regressions against main on 4 GPUs, and end-to-end training smokes match main's loss at every iteration. This branch itself ran only on 4 CPU gloo ranks: no regressions, 16 of the new tests pass, and the 5 seed test cases need CUDA. All 6 duplicate-filter mock tests pass.

**Compatibility.**
- On the standard grid, the seeds, the duplicate filtering and the checkpoint writers use the same groups and ranks.
- The fallbacks read group ranks. A rank forced with `set_tensor_model_parallel_rank` or the expert rank setters no longer replaces the group rank there. With `lazy_mpu_init`, which sets a provisional TP rank, the seed then uses the TP group rank. #8737 makes the same change for training and asks for sign-off on it. Checkpoint tools set rank overrides but neither seed nor call these filters.
- About 700 test calls of `model_parallel_cuda_manual_seed(123)` without a collection now warn once per process. They are not converted here. The snippet in `megatron/core/QuickStart.md` makes the same call.
- Without groups, the duplicate filters build a collection for every parameter, which is slower than one accessor call. In-repo optimizers pass their groups, so only hand-built optimizers and direct callers pay for it.
- `gtp_replica_rank`'s warning names the `explicit_group` argument, which the checkpoint path never passes. What is actually missing is `dp_cp` or `expt_dp` in the layer's collection. The `RuntimeError` text says so.
- #8764 stacks on this PR. With it, `resolve_gtp_remat_group` warns on its own and takes an `owner` argument, and `param_is_not_gtp_duplicate` and `model_parallel_cuda_manual_seed` pass `owner=None`, because they have already warned.
- Landing: this PR replaces #8734's duplicate-filter bodies with resolver-based ones and retargets its three mock tests. The warning text is unchanged.
- Needs `determinism-exempt`: `tensor_parallel/layers.py` is a registered kernel file. The changes there only plumb groups.

Part of #6307.

+"""Share one model-parallel state across the A2A overlap tests of a module.
+
+destroy_model_parallel() releases the fused A2A (DeepEP and HybridEP) buffers together with
+the process groups they communicate over, and building a HybridEP buffer takes tens of
+seconds. Initializing and destroying model parallelism around every test would rebuild the
+buffer for every HybridEP case. Tests request their layout through ``shared_model_parallel``
+instead. It keeps the current state while tests request the same layout, and destroys it when
+a test requests a different layout, when a test fails on any rank, and at the end of the
+module.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+import megatron.core.parallel_state as ps

+from tests.unit_tests.test_utilities import Utils, clear_nvte_env_vars
+
+# (layout, model-parallel group) of the state initialized through this module, or None.
+_shared = None
+
+
+def _destroy_shared():
+    global _shared
+    _shared = None
+    Utils.destroy_model_parallel()
+
+
+def _use_layout(**layout):
+    """Initialize model parallelism with ``layout``, reusing the current state if it matches."""
+    global _shared
+    clear_nvte_env_vars()
+    if (
+        _shared is not None
+        and _shared[0] == layout
+        and ps.model_parallel_is_initialized()
+        and ps.get_model_parallel_group(check_initialized=False) is _shared[1]
+    ):
+        return
+    if _shared is not None:
+        _destroy_shared()
+    Utils.initialize_model_parallel(**layout)
+    _shared = (layout, ps.get_model_parallel_group())
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def shared_model_parallel():
+    """Return a function that initializes model parallelism with the given layout.
+
+    Its keyword arguments are those of Utils.initialize_model_parallel. The state persists
+    across the module's tests while they request the same layout.
+    """
+    yield _use_layout
+    if _shared is not None:
+        _destroy_shared()
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def _reset_shared_model_parallel(request):
+    """Reset per-test state between tests that share model parallelism."""
+    failures_before = request.session.testsfailed
+    yield
+    if _shared is None:
+        return
+    # All ranks must agree on whether to destroy the groups, and a test can fail on a
+    # subset of ranks. Destroy them after any failure, so later tests start fresh.
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    failed = torch.tensor(
+        [int(request.session.testsfailed > failures_before)], device=torch.cuda.current_device()
+    )
+    torch.distributed.all_reduce(failed, op=torch.distributed.ReduceOp.MAX)
+    if failed.item():
+        _destroy_shared()
+        return
+    # The NCCL EP context is sized by the first dispatch that bootstraps it, so each test
+    # bootstraps its own, as it did when every test destroyed model parallelism.
+    nccl_ep_release_context()
+    torch.cuda.empty_cache()

+"""Tensor-parallel helpers read the global grid only when the caller omits its groups, and warn.

+back to the global parallel grid: the fallback emits a ProcessGroupFallbackWarning and selects
+the same ranks as the global accessors.

+    ColumnParallelLinear,
+    RowParallelLinear,

+    param_is_not_gtp_duplicate,
+    param_is_not_tensor_parallel_duplicate,
+)

+# (tp, ep, etp, gtp, egtp) grids with non-trivial ranks on every seeded axis of 4 ranks.

+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)

+
+def _fallback_messages(record):
+    return [str(w.message) for w in record if issubclass(w.category, ProcessGroupFallbackWarning)]

+
+def _initialize_seed_grid(tp, ep, etp, gtp, egtp):
+    if (
+        Utils.world_size < 4
+        or Utils.world_size % (tp * gtp)
+        or Utils.world_size % (etp * ep * egtp)
+    ):

+    Utils.initialize_model_parallel(
+        tensor_model_parallel_size=tp,
+        expert_model_parallel_size=ep,
+        expert_tensor_parallel_size=etp,
+        gtp_remat_size=gtp,
+        expert_gtp_remat_size=egtp,
+    )
+
+
+def _tracker_states():
+    return {name: state.clone() for name, state in get_cuda_rng_tracker().get_states().items()}
+
+
+def _assert_same_states(actual, expected):
+    assert actual.keys() == expected.keys()
+    for name, state in expected.items():
+        assert torch.equal(actual[name], state), name
+
+
+def _seed_from_global_accessors(seed):
+    """Seed with every rank and world size the global accessors give."""
+    model_parallel_cuda_manual_seed(
+        seed,
+        force_reset_rng=True,
+        tp_rank=parallel_state.get_tensor_model_parallel_rank(),
+        ep_rank=parallel_state.get_expert_model_parallel_rank(),
+        etp_rank=parallel_state.get_expert_tensor_parallel_rank(),
+        gtp_remat_rank=parallel_state.get_gtp_weight_remat_rank(),
+        egtp_remat_rank=parallel_state.get_expert_gtp_weight_remat_rank(),
+        gtp_remat_world_size=parallel_state.get_gtp_weight_remat_world_size(),
+        egtp_remat_world_size=parallel_state.get_expert_gtp_weight_remat_world_size(),
+    )

+
+def _param(*, expert=False):
+    param = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.empty(2))
+    if expert:
+        # allreduce=False marks a parameter that uses the expert topology.
+        param.allreduce = False

+"""In-tree code takes the global memory buffer from megatron.core.utils, not from parallel_state.
+
+Stdlib only. Run directly with ``python tests/unit_tests/test_global_memory_buffer_imports.py`` to
+avoid the GPU fixtures used when pytest collects the enclosing unit-test package.
+"""
+
+import ast
+import importlib.util
+import pathlib
+import unittest
+
+REPO_ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+PARALLEL_STATE = "megatron.core.parallel_state"
+# megatron.core exports parallel_state under its legacy name as well.
+PARALLEL_STATE_NAMES = {"parallel_state", "mpu"}
+BUFFER_FUNCTIONS = {
+    "get_global_memory_buffer",
+    "destroy_global_memory_buffer",
+    "_set_global_memory_buffer",
+}
+# Tests are not scanned: they exercise the parallel_state aliases on purpose.
+SCANNED_FOLDERS = ("megatron", "examples", "tools")
+
+
+def parallel_state_buffer_uses(source, package):
+    """Return the lines that take a buffer function from parallel_state.
+
+    ``package`` is the dotted package of the scanned file, used to resolve relative imports. A
+    name bound to the parallel_state module anywhere in the file counts in every scope.
+    """
+    tree = ast.parse(source)
+    modules = set()
+    lines = []
+    for node in ast.walk(tree):
+        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
+            modules.update(a.asname for a in node.names if a.name == PARALLEL_STATE and a.asname)
+        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
+            module = node.module or ""
+            if node.level:
+                module = importlib.util.resolve_name("." * node.level + module, package)
+            for alias in node.names:
+                if module == PARALLEL_STATE and alias.name in BUFFER_FUNCTIONS:
+                    lines.append(node.lineno)
+                elif module == "megatron.core" and alias.name in PARALLEL_STATE_NAMES:
+                    modules.add(alias.asname or alias.name)
+    for node in ast.walk(tree):
+        if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute) and node.attr in BUFFER_FUNCTIONS:
+            owner = node.value
+            if (isinstance(owner, ast.Name) and owner.id in modules) or (
+                ast.unparse(owner) == PARALLEL_STATE
+            ):
+                lines.append(node.lineno)
+    return sorted(lines)
+
+
+class TestParallelStateBufferUses(unittest.TestCase):
+    """The scan finds every spelling of the parallel_state aliases and nothing else."""
+
+    PACKAGE = "megatron.core.transformer"
+
+    def test_detects_parallel_state_aliases(self):
+        cases = [
+            ("from megatron.core.parallel_state import get_global_memory_buffer\n", [1]),
+            (
+                "from megatron.core.parallel_state import (\n"
+                "    destroy_model_parallel,\n"
+                "    destroy_global_memory_buffer,\n"
+                ")\n",
+                [1],
+            ),
+            ("from ..parallel_state import get_global_memory_buffer\n", [1]),
+            (
+                "from megatron.core import parallel_state\n"
+                "parallel_state.get_global_memory_buffer().get_tensor(shape, dtype, 'mpu')\n",
+                [2],
+            ),
+            ("from megatron.core import mpu\nmpu.destroy_global_memory_buffer()\n", [2]),
+            ("from .. import parallel_state as ps\nps._set_global_memory_buffer()\n", [2]),
+            ("import megatron.core.parallel_state as grid\ngrid.get_global_memory_buffer()\n", [2]),
+            (
+                "import megatron.core.parallel_state\n"
+                "megatron.core.parallel_state.get_global_memory_buffer()\n",
+                [2],
+            ),
+            (
+                "from megatron.core import parallel_state\n"
+                "def f():\n    return parallel_state.get_global_memory_buffer()\n",
+                [3],
+            ),
+        ]
+        for source, lines in cases:
+            with self.subTest(source=source):
+                self.assertEqual(parallel_state_buffer_uses(source, self.PACKAGE), lines)
+
+    def test_ignores_the_core_buffer_and_unrelated_buffers(self):
+        cases = [
+            "from megatron.core.utils import get_global_memory_buffer\nget_global_memory_buffer()\n",
+            "from megatron.core import utils\nutils.destroy_global_memory_buffer()\n",
+            "from ..utils import destroy_global_memory_buffer, get_global_memory_buffer\n",
+            "from .utils import get_global_memory_buffer\n",
+            "from megatron.core import parallel_state\n"
+            "parallel_state.destroy_model_parallel()\n"
+            "fsdp_utils.get_global_memory_buffer()\n",
+        ]
+        for source in cases:
+            with self.subTest(source=source):
+                self.assertEqual(parallel_state_buffer_uses(source, self.PACKAGE), [])
+
+
+class TestInTreeBufferUses(unittest.TestCase):
+    """Library, example and tool code use megatron.core.utils for the global memory buffer."""
+
+    def test_in_tree_code_uses_the_core_buffer(self):
+        paths = [path for folder in SCANNED_FOLDERS for path in (REPO_ROOT / folder).rglob("*.py")]
+        paths.extend(REPO_ROOT.glob("*.py"))
+        violations = []
+        for path in sorted(paths):
+            relative = path.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)
+            package = ".".join(relative.parent.parts)
+            source = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+            for line in parallel_state_buffer_uses(source, package):
+                violations.append(f"{relative}:{line}")
+        self.assertEqual(violations, [])
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
